Koi · car-cost ledger · design batch 2 · sheet 11

Record pages

Where "show the math" gets cashed in — every derived number states its own basis
DRAWS    wireframes §8.1 – §8.6
READS    spec §C6 · articles 1 & 4 · inv. 7 · 16 · 17
LEDGER  decisions.md §B7 · July 2026
DATE     2026-08-04
ONE SHAPE, SEVEN KINDS

icon + title + date → fact rows → computed → reliability → delete

The fact rows are what the user typed. The computed panel is what Koi derived, and it never appears without its basis — the interval, the inputs, and what was included.

That separation is the whole design. A page that mixed them would leave the user unable to tell which numbers they are responsible for and which Koi is.

WHICH KINDS EARN A COMPUTED PANEL
KIND
PANEL
Fuel
always — economy, or the honest reason there is none
Trip
always — derived km, both ≈ shares, the disclaimer
Odometer

Service
Expense
only when an odometer is attached — the delta alone
Note
never — nothing to derive, and no amount
Milestone
opens as a glance sheet, not a page
REFUSED, DELIBERATELY

No "part of July's 487,90 €" line, on any record page

The temptation is real and worth writing down as refused. A record page that names its share of a period turns a record into a lens, and gives one figure two homes.

That is the exact ambiguity the time-pages work exists to prevent. Records answer what happened; Insights answers over what period. Neither borrows the other's job.

01 · Fuel — the flagship

Two states of one page, plus the interval a missed fill broke. None is styled as an error.
§8.2 · MEASURED · 12 JULY · LIGHT
9:41

Repsol Tarragona 12 July 2026 · Golf GTI

COMPUTED

About your usual 6,85.

Delete this fill

History

Every number is checkable against the one below it. 35,75 ÷ 26,10 = 1,3697 → 1,370 €/L. 91.240 − 90.862 = 378 km. 26,10 ÷ 378 × 100 = 6,90 L/100km. The basis names the 2 July fill because economy measures full tank to full tank — not the 8 July service, which is the nearer reading.

Delete is critical text on the ordinary surface, alone at the foot behind a rule — 44 pt, hard to hit by accident, and the only red on the page. The tab bar stays: a record page is a pushed page inside whichever tab you came from, and keeping the bar is what distinguishes a push from a sheet (§D1). Back reads ‹ History here, but the same page pushes inside Insights or Home too.

The missing number is explained, not apologised for — and the page does the one useful thing an empty state can: it says where the litres went (into the next interval) and offers the single action that would recover the measurement.

Note not recorded in faint ink rather than a dash — a dash reads as a value that failed, and this field was simply never filled in.

The basis line is the article-4 payload

26,10 L over 378 km · since the 2 July fill is not decoration. It is the sentence that lets a user disagree with Koi — and the one that makes the difference between the fill's own 132 km delta and its 378 km economy interval legible instead of looking like a bug.

When partials fall inside the interval a fourth line appears: "Includes this fill and 1 partial before it." Their litres are in the numerator, and saying so is what keeps the arithmetic auditable.

A missed fill breaks the interval, and the page says so

COMPUTED
This interval isn't measured.
A fill was missed before this one, so the litres and the distance don't describe the same driving.
Your next full tank starts a fresh interval.

Never an interpolated dot, never a guessed figure. Koi knows the arithmetic would be wrong, refuses it, then explains in one sentence why — and when it recovers.

The reliability footer is not optional

It is the line that makes every average above it trustworthy. 2 full fills in a row. Economy is reliable. or 18 of 21 full. Averages shown as ≈. — the ≈ on every downstream figure traces back to this one sentence.

Edit is quiet; create has ceremony

The pencil opens the same capture surface, prefilled, and saves without the spring or the saved moment. On an edit the record's own reading and any folded twin are excluded from the monotonicity check — otherwise correcting a mistyped odometer would be blocked by the very value being corrected.

02 · Trip, odometer, note, milestone

The three kinds that carry no money, and the one that is not a page at all.
§8.5 · TRIP · THE DOUBLE-COUNT DISCLAIMER
Salou2 – 4 July 2026 · Golf GTI
232 km
Start90.862 km
End91.094 km
COMPUTED
Fuel share≈20,40 €
All-in share≈58,00 €
Already part of your totals. This is that drive's share.

The disclaimer lives here, where the number is read as a total — not on the capture sheet, where at your averages is the honest label. Both ≈ are load-bearing: this is a share of money already counted, which is why a trip's trailing figure in History is km.

Refused here: average speed, per-trip economy, a map. A 13-hour trip reading "57 km/h" is parked-time fiction, and a trip is a ledger record — two readings and a name — not surveillance.

§8.4 · ODOMETER · A DELIBERATE READING
90.828 km28 June 2026 · Golf GTI
Sourceentered by hand
Photonone
COMPUTED
+186 km
since the 12 June reading · 16 days
11,6 km/day over that stretch.

This reading has a page because it was deliberate. The 2 July reading does not — it was logged with a fill, so inv. 7 folds it into that fill's page and it never gets a row of its own. Same trail, different surface.

The delta measures against the previous trail reading — any kind, from any record — not against the previous manual one. One trail, one arithmetic.

§8.6 · NOTE · NO AMOUNT, EVER
Rattle from the near-side front wheel21 June 2026 · Golf GTI
Only over 60. Mention it at the next service.
Note · not counted in totals

The absence is stated where a reader would look for the number. That footer line is inv. 16 made visible — without it, a note is a record with a suspiciously blank amount; with it, a note is a note.

No computed panel, because there is nothing to derive. It joins no month whisper, no bar, no rate — and it is still a first-class record you can filter to, swipe and edit.

§8.6 · MILESTONE · A GLANCE SHEET, NOT A PAGE
Insurance renewed17 June 2026 · Golf GTI
InsurerMapfre
Premium412,00 €
vs last year+14,00 €
Koi recorded this from your policy. It isn't a July charge.
Open insurance & papers

A projection is not a record, so it does not get a record page. A fitted sheet keeps the ledger visible behind it, has no Save, no pencil and no Delete — you cannot edit a milestone, only the policy that produced it. Its one action goes to that policy.

The last line does the work the History row's meta started: it names the 412,00 € as a premium, not a charge in this month's total. Plan charges get the same treatment — a glance sheet reading "Set by your plan — open the car to change it."

Sheet 11 of batch 2. Next: 12 reminders and the vault · 13 onboarding. Service and expense pages are the fuel page minus the economy panel — the same shape, so they are not drawn separately; where they differ is only that their computed panel appears at all only when an odometer was attached.
